newsitem.title: GERMANY: SAP software group seen gaining from strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: SAP software group seen gaining from strong dollar.

text.p: European business software group SAP AG said Tuesday it expected sales to rise by 25 percent to 30 percent in 1997, although analysts were more optimistic because of the strong dollar.

The German company, whose shares have risen about 36 percent since the beginning of the year, also said pre-tax earnings would grow slightly more quickly than sales and said its first-quarter business was developing as expected.
"The increase in pre-tax profit should be one to two percentage points higher than the growth in sales," SAP board member Henning Kagermann told a news conference.
But analysts who follow the company's shares said rising sales in the United States could boost results even higher.

"We are a bit more optimistic than SAP's forecast," said Michael Bahlmann at M.M. Warburg & Co. in Hamburg. "They are not just a market leader in Germany. They have a lot of growth in the U.S. and Japan, and the strong dollar will help them."
Chief Executive Dieter Hopp declined to give an outlook for the full year, but said SAP expected first-quarter results to be "within the range of expectations."
SAP, whose R/3 software is used by companies to control manufacturing, personnel, accounting and other business data, did not plan any capital increase this year, Hopp said.
The company's shares closed floor trading up 50 pfennigs at 279 German marks ($165) on Tuesday. Last fall they fell to just above 200 marks ($118) after a surprise revenue drop in the third quarter.
SAP shares have the potential to rise to 330 marks ($195) over the next 12 to 18 months, Bank Julius Baer said in a report that gave the software maker a "buy/outperform" rating.
In 1996, favourable exchange rates boosted sales 58 million marks ($34 million) last year and operating earnings 18 million marks ($10.7 million), SAP said.
Its U.S. unit generated sales of 1.386 billion marks ($822 million), compared with 1.799 billion ($1.07 billion) in Europe, 465 million ($276 million) in Asia and 72 million ($43 million) in Africa.

As previously reported, SAP 1996 group sales were 3.72 billion marks ($2.2 billion), up 38 percent from the year before. Group net profit rose 40 percent to 567.5 million marks ($337 million), while profit on ordinary activities climbed 43 percent to 967.2 million marks ($574 million).
